quest.title: Encounter in the Woods
quest.description: Talk to Arakavi in Vanarana, which might help the groundwork for Festival Utsava.

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: It's Arama and the Golden Nara. You are so tall. But the silver one by your side...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? What about the silver one?

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: How should I put it... You must be able to squeeze into the narrowest tree hollows. How convenient!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Well, based on Nara customs, we should do introductions first. This is Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon. This is Arakavi. You guys shake hands.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You are a little lost, but you shake hands with Arakavi anyway...\nYou try not to use too much strength.\nArakavu's hand feels... interesting to the touch.

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: How fascinating. I've heard a lot about Nara before, but this is the first time I've ever touched one. It's a very special feeling!

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: It's been a long time since we last hosted a Nara here. Many seeds have grown into trees, and many stories have become legends. That Nara was a good Nara — or so we've heard.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} is good, too. Strong and brave, like a sapling sprouting out of a rock wall. And they are here to help Arana.

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: Ah, Arana... It's been a while since we last met. I hope all is well, and that the little Nara at Vimara Village are well, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You know the kids of Vimara Village?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: We all do! Arana came back and told us stories about the little Nara. Nara Iotham, Nara Bahram, and Narana are our friends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not sure that counts as "knowing someone"...

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: What counts, then? Do we need to "shake hands" after the "introduction" like Nara do?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: I know what Paimon means. Nara eat and look for "treasures" together. Then they know each other, right?

choices.text: It's not quite that simple, either...

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: As long as we know each other's stories, we know each other. This is because the Aranara's world is a place for songs and dreams.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Arakavi is right. As long as we hear about Nara {NICKNAME} through songs and see what Nara {NICKNAME} looks like through dreams, it'll count as knowing you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks that we can leave this aside for now... After all, we're already friends!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes. Since we're going to celebrate Festival Utsava, Arakavi needs to make some preparations!

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: That's true. We need the Bija, right? I've sent Arayasa, Aradasa, and Arasudraka to look for Ashvattha's Concourses.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Spot on! But Paimon's wondering... Why don't you guys know where these concourses are?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Ashvattha's Concourses are very, very sacred places. We don't usually go there. We would prefer to let the Vasara Trees sleep and dream, until all memories come together in Sarva.

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: The forest will remember. No good thing will ever fade away, and all suffering will come to nourish something beautiful...

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: Anyway, you can find Arayasa, Aradasa, and Arasudraka looking for Ashvattha's Concourses out there. Arama, you go and help them.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #I will. If Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon run into us in the forest, we can go adventuring together!

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: #Very well. Nice to have met you, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

choices.text: I eat and search for treasures with Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes! And we're not just "people who know each other," but the best of companions!

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: It was nice to meet you! When Festival Utsava comes, we shall sing together in happiness!
